title: Pilot study investigating the association between BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and graft-versus-host disease (GvHD)
summary:
The BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) is pathogenic in immunosuppressed patients, primarily those who have undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation or kidney transplantation. It causes three major diseases: BKPyV-associated hemorrhagic cystitis, BKPyV-associated nephritis, and micropapillary bladder carcinoma. These diseases are associated with significant morbidity and mortality, but there is currently no causal therapy available, and treatment strategies are limited to screening and reduction of immunosuppressive therapy. However, due to the low prevalence of these diseases, knowledge about them remains limited and continues to be derived mainly from retrospective studies. Our working group has been able to contribute to improving knowledge in this area with numerous clinical and translational studies, particularly in the field of allogeneic stem cell transplantation. 	

In addition, there has been controversy for years about whether there is a link between the virus and graft-versus-host disease in patients who have undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Furthermore, our working group has already hypothesized that BKPyV virus replication could be a general phenomenon in epithelia.

With this pilot project, we are therefore planning to take the first step toward answering the question of whether there is a connection between BKPyV virus replication and GvHD in patients who have undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation. From our previous clinical studies at Greifswald University Hospital, we were able to identify 12 patients who developed BKPyV viruria and/or viremia during the clinical study and from whom mucosal biopsies, particularly skin biopsies, were also taken and GvHD was detected.

interventions.name: Retrospective evaluation of allogeneic stem cell transplant patients with BKPyV viremia and/or viruria and evidence of GvHD; no comparison group; the histological sections of GvHD in these patients are examined for BKPyV using PCR, immunohistochemistry, and RNA in situ hybridization.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Within the studies (ethics votes BB 116/13 or BB 146/15) BKPyV viruria or viremia
- Histologically confirmed cutaneous GvHD and availability of paraffin blocks
Exclusion criteria:
None have been defined.
